_doc: Canonical fixtures cherry-picked from Phase 2.4 batches 10/11. Each fixture is one Test Cases sheet row that was deeply analyzed via explore agent and committed to torch_xpu_ops_issues.xlsx (resolve the XPU Case Exist / case_existence_comments columns by header name, not by index). The regression test re-asks the skill to classify the same row and verifies the verdict + that the explanation contains key tokens that prove the deep-analysis path executed.

fixtures.name: true_dtypesIfCUDA_intercept
fixtures.rationale: True only by way of the XPUPatchForImport intercept of @dtypesIfCUDA via get_dtypesIf_mock in xpu_test_utils.py:855-970,1143. Any classification not citing that mechanism is a regression of the deep-analysis logic.

fixtures.name: false_distributed_not_in_skip_dict
fixtures.rationale: False because test_tp_examples.py is not keyed in third_party/torch-xpu-ops/test/xpu/skip_list_dist.py skip_dict, so run_distributed.py never invokes it on XPU. Verdict must cite that distributed-harness routing.

fixtures.name: true_but_skipped_common_harness
fixtures.rationale: True-but-SKIPPED because the common (non-distributed) harness keys test_fake_tensor_xpu.py in third_party/torch-xpu-ops/test/xpu/skip_list_common.py skip_dict with value ('test_cudnn_rnn',); launch_test builds -k "not test_cudnn_rnn", so the generated test_cudnn_rnn_without_fallback variant IS collected but filtered out at runtime. A classifier that reads None/tuple skip semantics as whole-file-skipped, or that ignores skip_list_common.py for non-distributed tests, is a regression.
